calls.head: The Canucks can’t afford to take penalties
calls.body: The Canucks’ penalty kill is the league’s worst, and the Red Wings’ power play is one of the best. Discipline matters more than usual for the Canucks tonight.

calls.title: The Red Wings’ power play did its job
calls.plain: The Red Wings’ power play created at least its usual chances. Detroit went 1 for 4 on the power play.
calls.said: the Red Wings’ power play would get its usual chances against the Canucks’ shaky kill
calls.beyond: Detroit has one of the league’s most dangerous power plays, and Vancouver has one of the league’s leakiest penalty kills. Even by those standards, this was a big night: Detroit’s power play created 16.7 expected goals per 60, against their usual 8.9 (about 10.2 against Vancouver) and a league average of 7.6. A team strays this far about once every 20 games.

calls.head: The Red Wings’ edge in shot volume
calls.body: The Red Wings are around the middle of the league for shot volume, and the Canucks are one of the worst. It’s the widest gap between these two, though not a huge one.

surprises.head: Both teams played to type
surprises.body: Nothing in this game strayed far from how these two usually play: the shot share, the quality of chances, special teams, hitting, ice time and goaltending all landed inside their normal night-to-night range.

story.head: The Red Wings keep the Canucks winless in nine
paras: It was a busy first period. Lucas Raymond and William Wallinder scored less than two minutes apart early in the period to put the Red Wings up 2-0. Elias Pettersson (#40) got the Canucks on the board on the power play 58 seconds later. The Canucks went more than 39 minutes without a shot on goal, from early in the first to early in the third, even with a power play in that stretch. No team went that long without a shot on goal in any game of the three seasons before this one. Raymond scored again on the power play midway through the first to make it 3-1 for the Wings. Michael Rasmussen stretched the lead to 4-1 midway through the second. Michal Postava took over from John Gibson in net for Detroit to start the third. Emmitt Finnie made it 5-1 for the Red Wings early in the third, but Jonathan Lekkerimäki made a dent in Detroit’s lead midway through the period, bringing it to 5-2. J.T. Compher was back in the lineup after missing seven games, and picked up an assist. Raymond added an assist for a three-point night.

The Red Wings drove the play, outshooting the Canucks 31-13, and the scoreboard caught up. Kevin Lankinen allowed five goals on 31 shots for the Canucks. The Red Wings moved to 4-3-3, climbing off the bottom of the Atlantic, now sixth. The Canucks sank to last in the NHL. The Canucks are winless in nine (0-8-1).

items.text: The Red Wings have points in six straight games (3-0-3).
The Red Wings have beaten the Canucks four straight times, going back to the 2024-25 season.
Michael Rasmussen scored his first goal of the season, his first since Jan 5 (34 games played since).
Axel Sandin-Pellikka was in NHL.com’s projected lineup, but Anton Johansson played instead.
